open: [STUB] The market lines are noisy again at the Ring Two food stalls, and a stallholder slaps her receipt on the counter. The crew holds up a second receipt for the same order of forty bowls, paid for twice. She says it never left her stall. Rule before the bell, or the crew boycotts the counter and the Exchange clerk logs a complaint against whoever let it stand.

clean.text: [STUB] Onions fry somewhere above as the stallholder counts what a second batch of bowls would cost her, then nods at half the sum. The crew lead tears a receipt in two and drops one piece on her counter. Word of the fair split runs down the stall line before the bell. Two neighbours wave the crew over.

cost.text: [STUB] The stallholder takes a thousand credits from the crew, then stacks the still-warm bowls for them without a word. Both receipts go into her till, marked settled. The bell rings over a counter that stays quiet. The crew lead looks at the empty coin tray and leaves with the order.

fail.text: [STUB] The stallholder counts the offered half twice and pushes it back across the counter. The bell rings over two people still shouting about one order, and the crew files out with the boycott on. A neighbour calls after them that the registry desk by the Exchange hears disputes at first shift tomorrow. The shouting rings on in everyone's ears.

clean.text: [STUB] A loader argues with a scanner nearby while the crew's tech opens the scale housing and pulls its log. The log shows forty bowls leaving once, at the hour on the crew's receipt. The stallholder finds a duplicate stamp in her own book and tears the page out herself. The crew's shoulders drop.

cost.text: [STUB] The scale log shows the order left once, and the stallholder, caught out, counts five hundred credits into the crew's palm for the second receipt she cashed. Sorting two ledgers against the clock leaves everyone grey and short of breath. The bell is already tolling. She hands over the bowls anyway.

fail.text: [STUB] The scale reads true and her book reads clean, which settles neither receipt. The crew's tech cracked the scale housing prying it open, and five hundred credits go to the stall for the repair. The bell rings with both papers still in their pockets. A chandler points them to the notice board by the Exchange, where disputes are filed for first shift.

clean.text: [STUB] The clerk arrives with a stamp and a hand scanner and reads both receipts in a single pass. The older one is voided with a thump of the stamp, and the stallholder counts a thousand credits back into the crew's hands for the double charge. Her neighbours watch in silence. The bell rings on a finished order.

cost.text: [STUB] The clerk rules for the crew and bills a five-hundred-credit filing levy to whoever called for the ruling. The stallholder snaps a lid onto the last bowl and slides the full order across, glaring. The boycott is off. She will remember who sent for the clerk.

fail.text: [STUB] The clerk reads both receipts, sighs, and says the stamps match, so no ruling can come before the bell. The stallholder glares at the crew for sending for the clerk at all. The crew leaves with the boycott on. Tomorrow the clerk's own window on the Exchange floor will hear both papers, and the glare follows them out.

ending: [STUB] Hearthline's Ring Two stalls fall behind into the market din. The ledger card follows.
